late frame: the nurse shows a safe recovery position and points to a printed reminder card for parents

content.audio_transcript: If you have a baby, it helps to know a few first aid basics before you ever need them. First, stay calm and check whether your baby is responsive. If something feels wrong, call emergency services right away. Second, if your baby is choking, do not put your fingers in the mouth—follow infant choking steps from a certified class or trusted medical source. Third, keep a small emergency card on your fridge with your address, pediatrician, and allergy notes. A few minutes of preparation can make a huge difference.
